title: Non-local nonstabiliserness in Gluon and Graviton Scattering
summary: The property of non-stabiliserness, or ``magic'', is of interest in quantum computing due to its role in developing fault-tolerant quantum algorithms with genuine computational advantage over classical counterparts. There has been much interest in quantifying magic in various physical systems, in order to probe how to produce and enhance it. The production of magic has previously been quantified in gluon and graviton scattering, in the so-called helicity basis relating particle spins with momentum directions.
